**Gaps — no SOP yet**

• **Member Onboarding** – first 7 days post-sign-up (goal-setting call, intro class booking, nutrition baseline, payment setup confirmation). Critical revenue protection and retention lever.
• **Cancellation & Churn** – triggered exit interviews, pause-offer workflow, win-back cadence. Women's gyms see high emotional churn; need proactive salvage steps.
• **Member Check-ins** – 30/60/90-day touchpoints, progress tracking, upsell/referral prompts. Prevents silent churn.
• **Coaching Development Roadmap** – how coaches level up (certifications, niche specialism, retention milestones). No clarity = turnover.
• **Class Quality Audit** – monthly coaching standards review (form cues, pacing, energy, music, modifications offered). Protects brand and member outcomes.
• **Member Data Privacy & GDPR** – contact preferences, data retention, deletion requests, DPA breach protocol. Legal/compliance non-negotiable for UK gym.
• **Referral Programme** – mechanics, reward tiers, tracking, member comms. High ROI if friction-free.
• **Troubleshooting Guide** – common booking issues, payment fails, app glitches, complaint escalation paths. Reduces ad-hoc firefighting.

**Needs updating**

• **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – likely exists but unclear on: how feedback loops back to coaching standards, who owns quality audits, how performance is measured beyond attendance.
• **Milestone Achievements** – probably missing: how to celebrate wins (social media tagging, in-studio recognition), tie-in to referral triggers, nudge members towards next goal.
• **30 Day Goals** – needs clarity on: initial goal-setting SOP (who, when, how), how

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Audit what you're ACTUALLY selling right now**
- Have each coach list every service/offering they currently deliver (classes, PT, nutrition coaching, challenges, etc.). You'll find inconsistencies. Standardize these first before documenting anything. Don't create a menu for what you *think* you offer — crystallize reality.

**Price backwards from your unit economics**
- Calculate: monthly rent/operating costs ÷ target member count = minimum revenue per member needed. Then decide: are memberships pure revenue, or is PT/add-ons your profit driver? This determines if your menu emphasizes classes (sticky, recurring) or premium services (high-margin). Price the menu accordingly, not guesswork.

**Split into two radically different documents**
- **Member menu** (aspirational, benefits-focused): "6-week body confidence challenge" not "small group training sessions." Coaches sell outcomes, not services. Include what transformation looks like.
- **Coach menu** (operational, boundary-setting): pricing, package inclusions, cancellation policies, what's included in membership vs. what's add-on. This prevents scope creep and billing chaos.

**Test-drive with 5 members + 2 coaches**
- Share drafts separately, ask: "What's confusing? What would make you buy more?" Members will reveal language gaps; coaches will flag what's unsellable or unrealistic. Iterate before rolling out.

**Embed pricing psychology deliberately**
- Show 3 tiers minimum (entry/standard/premium). Most will pick middle. Bundle add-ons strategically (e.g., nutrition consultation free with 3-month PT package) to increase
